results.content: “The scale of needs in Gaza remains immense, and early recovery is critical to restoring the basic conditions that allow people to remain on or return to their communities with dignity,” said Jaco Cilliers, UNDP/PAPP Special Representative of the Administrator. “The Republic of Korea has been a critical partner in this effort. R.E.V.I.V.E II builds on what we have achieved together, connecting transitional shelter with essential services and neighbourhood-level interventions to support recovery [...] Building on these efforts, R.E.V.I.V.E II will contribute to UNDP’s broader Gaza Neighbourhood Programme, which brings together transitional shelter, debris removal, basic infrastructure, essential services and livelihoods support within the same communities. The approach aims to help Palestinians remain on or return to their areas of origin by progressively restoring the conditions that make neighbourhoods functional — connecting shelter with water and sanitation, health, education and [...] With an allocation of USD 7.76 million, R.E.V.I.V.E II builds on the achievements and lessons of the first phase, with a continued focus on transitional shelter, essential services and integrated neighbourhood-level recovery, helping create the conditions for Palestinians to remain on or return to their communities in safer and more dignified conditions.

results.title: WashU partners with St. Louis to expand CLEAN STL tornado recovery project - The Source - WashU
results.content:
Under the expanded partnership, WashU researchers will broaden soil testing efforts with additional community partners and establish a network of air-quality monitors in neighborhoods experiencing concentrated demolition activity. The monitors will provide neighborhood-level air-quality data to help track dust and contaminants during rebuilding efforts. WashU researchers will place 10 air-monitoring units around the city in the areas of highest demolition concentration. [...] The expanded initiative represents a significant investment of university resources, with WashU committing more than $500,000 over the next two years to support the project’s first phase of growth.  
  
The signees on the partnership were St. Louis Mayor Cara Spencer; Julian Nicks, chief recovery officer for the city; Victoria Anwuri, St. Louis health commissioner; and Dorian Traube, the Neidorff Family and Centene Corporation Dean of the WashU Brown School. [...] “St. Louis is moving into the next chapter of recovery, and that work has to be grounded in trust, transparency and good science,” Spencer said. “This partnership puts real-time information in the city’s and residents’ hands, brings world-class expertise to the neighborhoods that have waited too long for it, and shows that the rebuilding of north St. Louis is going to be done in a community-centric way.”
